scope: Uniquely owned S3 log bucket/object, single-region nonorganization trail, standard SQS queue, custom EventBridge bus, Lambda function and assume-only execution role. Advanced selectors contained only Data and exact owned queue/bus/function ARNs; management logging was never started. All owned AWS resources deleted and absence verified.
transport: AWS CLI 2.36.28 through scripts/aws/aws_cli.py; response-only debug extraction, no signing logs retained. Actual S3 .json.gz objects decoded in memory; only owned selector-resource records retained.
normalization: Account consistently replaced with 111111111111; source IPv4 replaced with documentation address; caller name/ARN normalized.
Access-key IDs, IAM principal IDs and SQS receipt handles replaced with stable SHA256-derived placeholders; signing secrets/tokens never retained.
Owned synthetic API input/response payloads redacted; native CloudTrail HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS, empty objects, omitted fields and explicit null fields are untouched.
Request IDs, event IDs, names, timestamps, region, ordering and native gzip hashes/sizes retained. Gzip files not retained because native contents include credential identifiers.
Source CLI action uses kebab-case; native eventName is untouched. API result shape and native Records remain separate; derived projection rules are not native records.

sqs.documented_special_case: ListQueues operates on no specific queue: CloudTrail resource ARN has wildcard * instead of queue name. The exact owned queue ARN selector deliberately does not admit that wildcard; the API call used only the exact owned QueueNamePrefix.

events.management_rule: All EventBridge API operations except PutEvents and PutPartnerEvents are management operations.
documented_conditions: Endpoint resource is populated only for successful global-endpoint PutEvents, not AccessDenied.
Data event delivery goes to the calling account, not automatically to resource-owner accounts.
PutPartnerEvents resource is the partner event source, not the customer bus.

lambda.distinction: InvokeExecution is an additional native AWSService record for asynchronous execution, not an API method inferred from the documentation table. LambdaESMDisabled is documented for supported event-source mapping failures; no mapping was created.

derived_projection_rules.rule: All retained owned-service records have eventCategory Data, managementEvent false and eventType AwsApiCall. Native eventName is preserved rather than mechanically generated from SDK action names.

Captured queue read APIs, including ReceiveMessage, have readOnly true and explicit responseElements null. Resources include accountId,type AWS::SQS::Queue,ARN. No received message payloads or receipt handles appear in responseElements.

SendMessage and SendMessageBatch readOnly false. Each request messageBody is HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS. Supplied messageAttributes becomes an empty object {}; absent messageAttributes stays omitted. Response includes native mD5OfMessageBody/mD5OfMessageAttributes/messageId casing, with batch successful entries rather than per-entry CloudTrail events.

Requested MessageAttributeNames [All] becomes messageAttributeNames [HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS]; messageSystemAttributeNames [All] remains. Other explicit receive limits/timeouts are retained. Only this one-element attribute-name form was exercised.

Single ChangeMessageVisibility/DeleteMessage have responseElements null; batch calls retain entries and successful/failed response arrays. Receipt handles are present natively in requests and have fixture-only stable redaction. Native successful result order can differ from input order; preserve service response order.

Partial batch failure remains HTTP200, with per-entry errors in responseElements and omitted top-level errorCode/errorMessage. Whole duplicate-ID failure records BatchEntryIdsNotDistinct, dropping HTTP protocol AWS.SimpleQueueService. prefix; responseElements null. Invalid receipt single request records ReceiptHandleIsInvalid and errorMessage.
Native requestParameters adds maxResults:0 although caller omitted MaxResults. No general default-insertion rule inferred.

PutEvents is one readOnly false Data record per HTTP request, with entries arrays. Every detail (including malformed detail) becomes HIDDEN_DUE_TO_SECURITY_REASONS. Source/detailType/resources/eventBusName retained; bus name vs ARN spelling preserved in entries. Top-level resources deduplicates this single bus and contains type/ARN but omits accountId; entry Resources is not a selector-resource list.

Native HTTP200 partial failure keeps responseElements.failedEntryCount:1 and mixed entries eventId or errorCode MalformedDetail/errorMessage. Top-level errorCode/errorMessage omitted; failed entry detail also suppressed.

Sync/Event/DryRun all produce exact eventName Invoke, readOnly false, responseElements null. requestParameters contains canonical function ARN and invocationType, no invocation payload. Resources includes accountId,type AWS::Lambda::Function,ARN. additionalEventData.functionVersion uses :$LATEST; synchronous sample also has customerEniId empty string.

Asynchronous Event produces both Invoke caller record and InvokeExecution AWSService record sharing the source HTTP request ID but distinct event IDs. InvokeExecution includes invokedBy/sourceIPAddress/userAgent lambda.amazonaws.com, requestParameters functionName/sourceArn/logType None/contentType application/json/sourceAccount, additionalEventData customerEniId empty/functionVersion, sharedEventID, and omits tlsDetails.

HTTP400 InvalidRequestContentException correlated Invoke event has explicit requestParameters null and responseElements null, and OMITTED errorCode/errorMessage/additionalEventData. Do not blindly project the HTTP error into the CloudTrail record.

limitations: Initial setup/first API observation list was lost due to a shared evaluator variable collision; no setup request IDs were fabricated. Every requested service operation was reissued with full response HTTP IDs after isolating state; all reissued operations except intentionally selector-excluded ListQueues have correlated native records. Earlier owned native events remain in gzip projections but may lack retained source-response correlations.

GetEventSelectors and a repeated PutEventSelectors preserve actual selector admission and show only exact owned Data resources. Initial Lambda create encountered role-propagation InvalidParameterValueException before succeeding; initial setup response not retained after evaluator collision.

ListQueues native record unobserved under exact queue selector; documented wildcard ARN was not selected because doing so would enable logging for nonowned list activity. API prefix limits results only, not CloudTrail selector identity.

No FIFO queue, partner event source, global endpoint, event-source mapping, cross-account or cross-region data operation exercised. No universal projection behavior inferred beyond documented vocabulary and actual records.

Role had only Lambda assume-role trust, no attached or inline permissions; handler returned a constant and emitted no customer payload. No CloudWatch log groups found for the exact owned Lambda prefix.

Raw CLI invocation/get-object initially rejected cli-input-json-only forms because custom CLI commands require explicit flags; successful reissue used explicit --function-name/--bucket/--key and is the correlated evidence.
